proposals.whyCommon: Large tech, finance, and consumer companies run structured summer data science internship programs every year, making it one of the most recognizable data intern titles.
requiredSkills: Python or R for analysis and modeling
SQL for pulling and joining data

candidateEdges.rationale: This is the direct feeder role; the intern does scoped-down versions of a data scientist's daily modeling and analysis work.
The modeling and ML-fundamentals overlap is real, and many DS interns move toward ML engineering; an advisor would nod at the adjacency.
Shared statistical-inference and experiment foundations make this a plausible bridge, though the DS role is broader and less rigor-focused.

proposals.whyCommon: Companies with large data platforms staff dedicated data engineering internships to build pipelines and warehouse tooling, a standard early-careers track at scaled tech and finance firms.
requiredSkills: Cloud data platforms (AWS, GCP, or Azure)
Data modeling and schema design basics

candidateEdges.rationale: Direct feeder role; the intern builds and maintains pipelines and schemas that are the core of the data engineer job.
Data modeling and warehouse-schema exposure is the shared foundation; both roles map to the same SOC (15-1243.00), so an advisor would affirm the path.
Interns constantly build the clean datasets and SQL that analysts consume, a genuine but weaker adjacency.

proposals.whyCommon: AI-focused startups and scaleups hire ML engineering interns heavily to help ship models to production, and the title is widely recognized across the industry.
requiredSkills: Machine learning fundamentals and model evaluation
Linear algebra, calculus, and probability foundations
Working with messy or high-volume datasets
Clean, efficient coding and version control

candidateEdges.rationale: This is the direct feeder role; the intern trains, evaluates, and ships models exactly as the ML engineer does.
Modeling and dataset-analysis overlap is substantial; DS and ML intern pipelines frequently share the same teams and skills.
Building training pipelines and handling large data at scale gives honest overlap with data engineering that an advisor would recognize.

proposals.whyCommon: Retail, finance, and CPG companies routinely run BI and analytics internships to build dashboards and reporting, a staple entry point into the data field.
requiredSkills: BI and dashboarding tools (Tableau, Power BI, or Looker)
Business metric definition and KPI reporting

candidateEdges.rationale: Direct feeder role; the intern builds the dashboards and periodic reports that define the BI analyst job.
SQL, dashboarding, and stakeholder-reporting overlap is heavy; the two roles are often interchangeable at the intern level.
Analytics interns touch experimentation and metric analysis that lead toward data science, a real but lighter adjacency.

proposals.whyCommon: Airlines, logistics, supply-chain, and consulting firms run operations research and optimization internships to model and improve real operational decisions.
requiredSkills: Linear / integer programming and simulation basics

candidateEdges.rationale: Direct feeder role; the intern formulates and validates optimization/simulation models that are the operations research analyst's core work.
Shared reliance on probability, sampling, and rigorous model validation makes this an honest neighbor an advisor would affirm.
Quantitative modeling and data-driven recommendation work overlaps meaningfully with data science, though OR is more optimization-focused.

searchHints: American Airlines OR UPS operations research intern

proposals.whyCommon: Pharmaceutical, insurance, and government organizations run statistics and biostatistics internships to support experimental design and rigorous data analysis.
requiredSkills: R or Python (or SAS) for statistical analysis

candidateEdges.rationale: Direct feeder role; the intern applies statistical methods, designs analyses, and reports findings exactly as the statistician does.
Statistical foundations and experiment analysis carry directly into data science, a bridge both students and advisors recognize.
Shared statistical-inference, sampling, and model-validation skills make operations research an honest adjacent path.
